title: Parking lot requirements
idea: Scoping a parking lot system means fixing the actors, the entry, pay and exit use cases, which vehicles fit which spots, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Drivers take a ticket at entry, pay, then leave through an exit gate.
The core rule: one spot holds at most one vehicle at a time.
Each vehicle type fits only some spot types; a truck needs LARGE.
Assume several floors, hundreds of spots, and several gates working at once.

edges.caption: A driver arrives at an entry gate. The gate issues a ticket with an assigned spot.
Before leaving, the driver pays for the stay. The fee depends on vehicle type and time.
The exit gate opens only for a paid ticket. The spot becomes free again.
The system is an actor too: it keeps free-spot counts on the display boards.

edges.label: lost ticket
edges.caption: An attendant handles a lost ticket and charges a fixed lost-ticket fee.
Advance booking, monthly passes and EV charging wait for later. Say the cut out loud.

code.title: Use cases and fit rules
code.caption: The scope as code: each use case has an actor and a v1 flag, and each vehicle type lists the spots it may use.

walk.text: Print every use case with its actor, tagged v1 or later.
Print the fit rule: which spot types each vehicle type may use.
Three actors: the driver, the attendant, and the system itself.
A bike fits anywhere, a car needs COMPACT or LARGE, a truck needs LARGE.
Five use cases make v1, including lost tickets for the attendant.
Reservations, passes and EV charging are listed, so the cut is visible.

pitfalls: Agree on the fit rule early; it drives allocation, pricing and the schema.
State traffic and size numbers as assumptions, not as measured facts.
Name lost tickets and failed payments now; they shape the ticket lifecycle.

quiz.q: Where should a spot be chosen in the v1 parking lot?
options: By the driver, who parks in any free spot
At the entry gate, when the ticket is issued
At the exit gate, when the fee is paid
In advance, through a reservation screen
quiz.why: Assigning at entry lets the system enforce the fit rule and one vehicle per spot, and keeps free counts exact. Reservations are out of scope.

takeaway: Fix actors, use cases, fit rules and cuts before drawing classes.

starters: Should drivers choose their own spot instead of the gate assigning one?
